summary.intent: Drive the caliper perf/correctness work to completion: land the fallback-off lane (#464), resolve review findings on the Storybook live-upgrade PR (#462), and get the user to rethink the patch-per-finding approach.
summary.outcome: #464 merged and main CI is green. #462 got a fix for the subcomponent watch finding, but a new eager-session diagnostics finding (session.ts:272) led the user to demand a root-cause step back, so a redesign worker (reducer, single decision owner, model-based test) is running. Resolver deletion, a real storybook dev demo, quiet-machine measurement and the oracle run remain.

repo: With the structural fallback off, 251 of 252 suite rows pass; generics/29 (indexed access) is a documented checker limit, returned as a typed `opaque` with `degradedBy` and a warning, listed with a "limit" reason.
The oracle lane now fails any row that leans on the structural fallback unless it is a listed checker limit.
`ResolverFacts::ready` must request all descriptions when the fallback is off; the 4 silent rows existed because the checker was never asked for descriptions the structural pass already had.

The Rust core already merges structural and checker diagnostics (`drop_superseded`) and knows when the checker is pending; the TypeScript Storybook package re-derives both, which causes recurring findings.

Storybook lifecycle state is scattered flags across preset.ts, session.ts, provider.ts and background.ts (`open`, `replaced`, `watching`, `awaiting`, `answeredAway`); the #462 findings come from keying by component only instead of component+revision+key+client.

Resolver modules no longer read by the lane: alias, ambient, deps, extends, func, html, precedence, primitives, react, substitute, template, collected. memo, named, callee, chain, evaluate and module resolution are still referenced from outside resolver/.
PR status/findings are tracked with `entire trail` (link, finding list, finding resolve) alongside gh; Entire Gates shows BLOCKED on new PRs.

code.finding: Guard suppressed watches for subcomponents first requested by the refresh. Fixed in 32dae0c4: subcomponents are asked before the parent, and `replaced` is a per-component map of revision plus already-reported keys.
Throws on pending-parent fallback before the subcomponent loop (lines 234-237), so the first watch covers only the parent.

With `lazy: false`, this uses the structural index's diagnostics instead of the checker-refined ones from `sessionComponentAnswers`, so provider.ts:176-181 keeps falling back and ignores new checker warnings.

workflow: After the third review finding on a PR, stop spot-fixing: tabulate the findings, name root causes, and consider a redesign. This was saved to memory.
Call caps of 25-35 suit mechanical work but are too tight for stateful mechanisms; use a higher cap with permission to restructure.
Ask 'is the same fact decided or held anywhere else?' (one decision, two owners) before accepting a worker's fix.
Subagent hand-back reports should be verified against source, e.g. by checking ls-remote heads and diffs, before resolving findings.

friction: Eleven review findings on #462 across four-plus rounds, each a spot fix; the user was disappointed that the assistant did not step back sooner.
The assistant had said it would ask for a model-based approach if another finding appeared, then routed the next one as a spot fix anyway.
Someone merged main into the feature branch while a worker was running, requiring an extra merge.
Entire Gates shows BLOCKED on PRs, hiding the real merge state.
Earlier performance numbers were taken under load and never re-run on final main.
open_items: #462: finish the redesign (spec, single reducer, core-owned merged answer, model-based test), then verify the source and resolve the open session.ts:272 finding.
S7c-S7e resolver deletion: trace the remaining callers, delete the unread modules and their tests, move the needed plumbing, and confirm identical output. Use one worker with a tight brief.
Run a real `storybook dev` browser demonstration of the live upgrade.
Quiet-machine measurement: Storybook first answer is ~115-159 ms against a 150 ms target, watch ~164 ms p95 against 25 ms.
Oracle run, after the resolver deletion; cost is the user's call.
Release PR #396 is clean and waiting on the user, as is #462 once the redesign lands.
